newsitem.title: UK: Euro naphtha demand for gasoline seen set to rise.
newsitem.headline: Euro naphtha demand for gasoline seen set to rise.

text.p: Naphtha requirements for gasoline production are expected to rise in the short to medium term as traders expect gasoline's premium over naphtha will continue to improve.

"The gap is still relatively narrow, but market interest is starting to come in from gasoline players for naphthenic and aromatic naphtha," one trader said, as a U.K. major indicated it may seek N+A volumes.

Traders and brokers on Wednesday saw the trend of a growing premium unleaded gasoline cargo differential over naphtha established since July 18 - when the spread reached a low of $2.50 - being maintained, especially in the prompt physical market and on front month swaps.

By end Tuesday, the CIF NWE mogas/naphtha spread had risen to $10-$11 a tonne, although this compared to $32.00 back on May 23 and $18.50 on July 3, and was well short of the $20-$30 margin normally considered economic for reforming naphtha into mogas at refineries.

Refiners and traders saw no early signs that naphtha production, which has been maximized over recent weeks due to naphtha's strong position against crude and other oil products, would be reined in to make way for more gasoline output.

But traders did say that the widening, but still narrow, differential had begun by early Wednesday to generate interest in purchasing of naphthenic and aromatic naphtha - used for reforming into gasoline.

Euroil monthly refinery statistics for the European Union plus Norway published on Tuesday showed a 1.1 percent rise in overall June refinery output over May as gasoline production rose by just 0.2 percent but naphtha was up by 1.8 percent.
Naphtha production this June was 14.8 percent up on June of 1996, according to the statistics.

The maximization of naphtha output, which is seen to have continued through July, had been linked to strong European demand for petrochemical cracking after conclusion of a second quarter round of major turnarounds.

A wide mogas/naphtha differential during late May/June also encouraged strong demand for N+A naphtha, while the sustained strength since early July has been largely linked by dealers to an open arbitrage window for naphtha from the Mediterranean to both East Asia and the U.S. Gulf.

The arbitrage to Asia in particular, in part caused by recent production problems at a Thai splitter and by the restart of some of Asia's large-scale petchem crackers, was seen prompting large-scale Med-to-Asia fixtures for the July/August time-frame.

The resulting naphtha gains, which some products players now say was overdone and was long due for its current partial correction, saw the naphtha physical crack against Dated Brent rise from $37 a tonne on July 3 to over $54 by July 18, before retreating to $48-$49 by end-Tuesday.

The retreat has been linked to a markedly less bullish Asian market that has seen the Med-Asia arb once again closed, with the arb to the U.S. Gulf only seen working under special shipping conditions.

Moreover, the tendency over recent months of propane values to remain above naphtha - bucking a usual summer trend of lower propane than naphtha - has over the past week or two given way to virtual parity between the two products.
Propane is the main petchem feedstock alternative to naphtha in western Europe, and normally becomes widely attractive for cracking when it declines to 90-95 percent of the value of naphtha.
Traders and end-users see the likely downward direction of crude futures in the short term and naphtha's own fundamentals pointing to a weaker naphtha scene over coming weeks.
"Naphtha is showing definite signs of weakening due to the lack of buying interest and due expectations of falling crude levels," an NWE trader said.

By contrast, the lack of refinery availability of gasoline at a time of reasonable barge and cargo requirements in the Med and the north, has been seen pushing up gasoline values amid expectations that values will remain firm and parhaps rise further.

"Naphtha has been much too strong, due to speculation, but is now slowing down, while gasoline is staying quite firm," a Benelux refiner said, arguing that fresh support for gasoline could come from the arb to the U.S. Gulf.

Dealers in the U.S. expected gasoline demand and pricing to remain strong in the near term. Having been seen to underperform over recent months, U.S. dealers now expect gasoline to overperform against crude and heating oil, with many believing the U.S. driving season has yet to peak.
They've also seen persistently high prices of methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE), a leading gasoline component, pressuring reformulated gasoline prices in an upward direction.
